name: Wheat Leaf Streak Mosaic Virus
symptoms: Streaks of yellowed, non-uniform discoloration on leaves Stunted growth Severe infections can cause 100% crop loss Symptoms often more severe when synergistic infections occur with Triticum mosaic virus or High plains virus
management: cultural: Destroy volunteer wheat at least 2 weeks before planting new winter wheat Avoid early planting to reduce exposure to mites Select wheat varieties with lower susceptibility to WSMV chemical: Miticides are not effective against the wheat curl mite for controlling virus spread resistance: Use resistant/tolerant wheat cultivars where available Research on RNAi-based resistance is ongoing
sources: Seifers DL et al., 2002. Wheat streak mosaic virus: An Overview. Plant Disease 86: 781–790.
Martinez et al., 2019. Wheat curl mite-virus interactions. Front. Plant Sci.
USDA-ARS research on WSMV and vector biology.
